title: Control Panel Probe & Backlog Synthesis (Jun 2026)
content:
Context and goal:
This doc captures the exploratory usability probe we ran for the new control-panel (internal name: CP-2) surface, a lightweight synthesis of participant feedback, quick wireframe notes, and a prioritized backlog for next two sprints. The aim: validate whether the new grouped-actions pattern reduces cognitive load for multi-route debugging and to collect concrete changes we can ship before the beta release to Dedicated customers.

Participants and sessions:
- 8 moderated remote sessions (45–60m) with product/platform engineers at seed/series-B startups and two mid-market platform teams (4 external, 4 existing Redwood customers).
- Session script focused on three tasks: 1) identify why a route is overbudget (cost spike), 2) rollback a model rollout to previous version, 3) debug a 502 spike and find relevant logs/traces.
- Prototype used: mid-fidelity Figma (flow + a single interactive modal). Prototype link recorded in GH-frontend#3421.

Top-level findings (evidence-backed):
1) Action discoverability: participants expected primary actions (rollback, pin version, view perf) on the route row; hiding them behind a kebab menu increased task time by ~25% and caused 3/8 participants to hesitate. Quote: “I don’t want to open anything — show me rollback right there.”
2) Error context mismatch: the trace/log preview is too terse — engineers wanted one-line cause hints (e.g., "OOM on decode kernel") and a quick link to the full trace. Without the hint they clicked multiple places to confirm.
3) Cost attribution confusion: the default cost view aggregates model + infra and the label makes it hard to see per-token driver; participants asked for a toggle and a tooltip explaining the calculation.
4) Model rollouts mental model: people think of rollouts as a timeline. The current percentage slider felt abstract; participants preferred a discrete canary step (1%, 5%, 25%, 100%) with a labeled state history.
5) Undo and safety: rollback needs to show recent prompts/queries sampled and whether they contain PII; two customers flagged compliance need for auto-sampling policy display.

Quick wireframe notes (annotations for engineers/designers):
- Primary row affordances: make 3 actions visible on hover and optionally exposed on compact rows: [Rollback][Pin][Open Trace]. Keep kebab for secondary ops (rename, archive).
- Inline one-line cause preview: add a small status chip under the route name with color-coded severity and a 50–80 char hint (pulled from last 3 logs via scoring).
- Cost toggle: top-right of cost card -> default = "Total cost" with secondary toggle to "Per-token / Per-request". Include small help icon with calculation snippet.
- Rollout widget: replace freeform % slider with segmented stepper: 0 -> 1 -> 5 -> 25 -> 100. Each step stores timestamp and operator. Add small "view history" dropdown.
- Sampling & compliance panel: modal on rollback that shows a random sample of 5 requests in plaintext (redacted) and a notice if any requests flagged by DLP. Link to customer KMS retention policy.

Concrete backlog (prioritized with rationale) — rollout-ready items first:
P0 (next sprint):
- CP-1023: Expose [Rollback][Pin][Open Trace] on route row hover and keyboard accessible (acceptance: actions fire same API calls as kebab). Rationale: reduces task time, repeated request by beta customers.
- CP-1045: Add one-line cause preview chip under route title, populated from top-scored log message. Rationale: improves first-click resolution.

P1 (sprint +1):
- CP-1051: Replace % slider with segmented rollout stepper + history (backend ledger + UI). Acceptance: UI shows past rollouts with operator and timestamp; rollback to previous state possible within 24h. Rationale: aligns with user mental model, reduces errors.
- CP-1068: Cost card toggle and help tooltip; update docs. Rationale: addresses attribution confusion.

P2 (future):
- CP-1080: Rollout safety modal that samples requests and checks DLP; plumb to compliance flags. Rationale: regulatory ask from 2 customers.
- CP-1095: Quick trace—expand inline preview to 3 frames and latency breakdown. Rationale: deeper debug capability, lower noisy navigation.

Acceptance criteria (sample) for CP-1023: 
- Keyboard access: actions reachable via tab and have clear aria labels.
- Telemetry: average task completion time for rollback reduced by >=20% in internal bench study.
- No regressions introduced for compact row layout (QA across 3 breakpoints).

Open questions / risks:
- Data volume and perf: can the cause chip be populated without creating N+1 queries for high-cardinality traces? Engineering note: consider precomputed "top_hint" sampled in ingestion pipeline (Tess to follow up with infra).
- Access control: who can rollback in multi-tenant accounts? We need to map UI affordance to role checks (customer RBAC + org-level policy).
- SLO impact: exposing extra actions increases API surface; ensure rate-limits and circuit-breakers in place.

Proposed experiment (AB):
- Hypothesis: Exposed primary actions on route rows reduce mean time-to-rollback and increase confidence score (self-reported) without increasing accidental rollbacks.
- Variants: Control (current kebab-only) vs Variant A (exposed actions on hover) vs Variant B (exposed actions always visible on wide view).
- Metrics: time-to-first-action, rollback success rate, accidental rollback rate (confirmation cancelled), NPS-ish confidence rating in post-task survey.
- Target: run with 50 internal participants + 3 pilot customers over 2 weeks.

Design/engineering notes and quick wins (can ship in a day):
- Add tooltip copy explaining cost calc on hover (docs+copy only).
- Wireframe small status chips using existing color tokens.
- Add keyboard-only keyboard shortcut mapping: R = rollback quick-open for selected route (keybinding opt-in).

References and artifacts:
- Prototype: GH-frontend#3421 (Figma embed)
- Research notes raw recordings: S3 link (internal) and session transcripts in drive folder (link in CI).
- Related tickets: RDW-2147 (cost calculation), CP-1018 (trace preview work).

Next steps / owners:
- Aisha: finalize copy for status chips and rollout step labels (due: 2026-06-28).
- Marco: prototype the hover affordances and push demo branch (due: 2026-07-02).
- Tess: spike on "top_hint" precompute perf and cost (due: 2026-06-30).
- Ravi: map RBAC checks and add acceptance criteria for role gating (due: 2026-06-29).

Notes to self / rough todo: 
- Add quick wireframe screenshot snippets inline (TODO: export from Figma).
- Follow up with legal on sampled request redaction rules.
- Prepare 2-week pilot plan for variant A with beta customers.

Appendix — sample participant quotes (verbatim):
- "I expected rollback to be one click. Hiding it felt like you were trying to hide the power."
- "Show me a one-line cause. I can read full trace after I make a guess."
- "Segmented rollouts are how we think — a slider feels like gambling."

End of doc.
